title: Prove named-pipe framing and reconnect
starting_commit_note: The supplied bootstrap workspace is not a Git checkout; authority, dispatch, manifest, source, and evidence hashes are used as immutable identities.

prerequisites.required_output: Repository skeleton, pinned .NET/Node toolchains, deterministic settings, and isolated prototype paths

global_invariants: Only a local current-user client and the required Local System recovery identity may open the proof pipe.
Every frame has a four-byte big-endian length and strict UTF-8 JSON payload bounded before allocation.
One connection has one reader and one serialized writer; publisher work never blocks on an unbounded subscriber queue.
Durable event sequence is monotonic across server restart and replay is cursor-based with explicit truncation.
Node pipe access remains in a host process fixture and is not exposed to a webview package.
Prototype projects remain isolated and are not referenced by production projects.

acceptance.result: The live pipe security descriptor is protected and grants full access only to the current user SID and Local System; anonymous access is denied with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED.
acceptance.verifier: Live-handle DACL inspection and anonymous-token negative probe

acceptance.result: .NET and Node clients produce semantically identical handshake, Unicode echo, cancellation, subscription, replay, and incompatible-version outcomes.
Fragmented headers/bodies and coalesced frames are reconstructed; malformed JSON, invalid framing, and oversized lengths fail closed.
acceptance.verifier: Deterministic tests and Windows raw-pipe scenario

acceptance.result: The event cursor and journal survive a forced server restart and a Node subscriber reconnects without duplicate or non-increasing event delivery.
acceptance.verifier: Forced process restart with one persistent state directory

acceptance.result: A slow subscriber cannot exceed the declared subscription, event, or control queue capacities and is disconnected with a resume cursor.
acceptance.verifier: High-volume paused-reader scenario and final server metrics

expected_outputs: Strict transport-neutral protocol and framing libraries
Durable monotonic event journal, bounded server queues, subscriptions, cancellation, and replay
Explicit Win32 named-pipe creation, DACL readback, and negative identity probe
.NET and Node client fixtures plus reconnect support
Windows harness, scenario manifest, evidence schema, run script, proof document, source validator, and receipt
discretion: Internal helper class and file names may change while preserving protocol and evidence semantics.
Queue implementation may change only if all capacities remain declared, measured, and fail closed.
No production RPC, daemon, UI, scheduler, database, or adapter contract may be introduced by this proof.
stop_conditions: Node named-pipe behavior cannot preserve framing, replay, reconnect, or strict schema semantics.
The explicit current-user DACL cannot be verified deterministically on the live pipe handle.
A slow client can cause unbounded retained memory or block durable event publication indefinitely.
Restart cannot preserve a monotonic durable event cursor.
A required change would reference prototype code from a production project.
